claims.text: The initial material is cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr is highly susceptible to oxygen and has poor high-temperature oxidation resistance.
3D ink extrusion printing followed by hydrogen de-binding and titanium-sponge-gettered vacuum sintering will reduce oxygen uptake during processing.
Reduced oxygen uptake during processing will improve the alloy's high-temperature oxidation resistance.
The proposed processing route will preserve the alloy's inherent mechanical properties.
The proposed processing route will produce a refined microstructure.
Gettered vacuum sintering will reduce grain-boundary oxygen segregation.
Gettered vacuum sintering will lower the alloy's overall oxygen content.
Hydrogen de-binding removes organic residues that could introduce oxygen.
Titanium sponge acts as an oxygen getter during vacuum sintering.
The resulting cleaner alloy microstructure resists oxidation.
The fine microstructure produced by the printing route helps maintain room-temperature ductility.
The fine microstructure produced by the printing route helps maintain high-temperature strength.
Relative to cast material, treated material will have a lower oxidation rate during exposure at 1000 °C in an oxidizing atmosphere for about 12 hours.
Relative to cast material, treated material will incorporate less oxygen during exposure at 1000 °C in an oxidizing atmosphere for about 12 hours.
Relative to cast material, treated material will retain comparable or better room-temperature tensile ductility.
Relative to cast material, treated material will retain comparable or better yield strength at 1000 °C and strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.

contradictions.description: The conditions state that mechanical testing occurs while samples are exposed at 1000 °C for 12 hours, whereas the experiment states that mechanical testing is performed subsequently, after the oxidation exposure.

Lower oxidation rate is a predicted outcome and part of the falsification rule, but the listed measurements do not include mass gain, scale growth, oxygen flux, or another direct oxidation-rate measurement.
